items.title: The analysis's own debug-profile stack baseline under the walk is ~636 KB — `analyze_inner`'s frame alone is 214 KB unoptimized, `analyze_over_world` 83 KB, `analyze_source_unfenced` 79 KB, and four `catch_unwind` layers ~28 KB each move the 9.4 KB `Program` (and the 9.5 KB `AnalyzedEntry`) by value — so after N169 it is 70% of what the 1.5 MiB canary measures
items.body: Read with gdb at the canary's overflow on the v0.48.0 base (the table and the gdb script in the find). N169 took the walk's 33 levels from 0.89 to 0.26 MiB; the ~636 KB under the first level did not move and is now the larger share of the canary's ~0.9 MiB need, and it is the same on every analysis thread in the debug suite (the libtest 2 MiB workers the Windows shard has aborted on twice). Doors: (a) `analyze_inner` and `analyze_over_world` are one frame each over every phase's locals — the phases out of line as `#[inline(never)]` helpers, the walk's own rule (`walk_expr_node_inner`'s doc); (b) box the `Program` through the `catch_unwind` layers (`Option<Box<Program>>` inside `analyze_source_unfenced`), so each layer moves 8 bytes instead of ~28 KB. Measure: the per-frame table again, and the canary's threshold (N169 left it at ~900 KiB). Not urgent: optimized frames are a small fraction and nothing a user runs is near the cliff. Sizing S–M; the analyzer core's (after S7).

items.discussion: incr-51a (Order 51), E294's measurement; `vilan-lsp`'s `base_cache_budget_walk_across_a_sibling_checkout` over a lucide-carrying kolt copy, release, loadavg ~10
items.title: M67's 192 MiB budget no longer holds kolt's working set: its own focus-walk sweep misses 20 of 20 on the scan and 29 of 30 on the working set (M67 recorded 17 / 19 and 21 / 30) — the cache keeps two worlds, because kolt's worlds grew to ~74 MB each
items.body: Measured at E294 with the sweep's own harness (`VILAN_PERF_KOLT=<copy> VILAN_M67_BUDGET_MIB=192 cargo nextest run --release -p vilan-lsp --run-ignored ignored-only -E 'test(base_cache_budget_walk_across)' --no-capture`), with `VILAN_E294_SESSION=0` for M67's flat policy: `worlds` reads 2 at almost every visit, `weight` ~120–196 MiB, every scanning visit a miss (the opening visits are misses by construction). With E294's session sizing (the server's policy since this order) the walk keeps two more (the entries') and misses 18 / 20 scanning and 27 / 30 on the working set, at ~140 MB more resident. The 192 MiB figure was set by M67's table on a smaller kolt and on std as it was; it now buys almost nothing on the walk. Door: re-run the sweep at 0 / 192 / 256 / 384 / 512 MiB on today's kolt and re-rule the flat figure — or wait for std-prefix.md's P1/P2, which turn a miss into a package-only rebuild and change what a miss costs (the ruling should say which). Sizing S (a measurement and a ruling).
